categories.name: It works
categories.notes: dotnet build: 0 errors, 0 warnings (5/5). / returns 200 and is the Blog front page: title, intro, a block-grid text block, then both posts as cards with listing image, date, title link, excerpt and 'Read the post'. Both links return 200 (10/10). Both posts render all five blocks (3 text, 1 image with credit caption, 1 quote) with no 'Could not render component' (10/10). Four provided Unsplash photos are imported into a 'Blog' media folder and served through signed GetCropUrl URLs, 4/4 load (5/5). The domain '/' is on the Blog front page, not WWW, and all three pages are published (5/5).

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: textBlock, imageBlock and quoteBlock are elements in Blocks. frontPage and blogPost are documents in Pages, and siteRoot stays in Repositories (8/8). 'Blog Body Blocks' allows rich text (RTE), image (media picker + caption) and quote (quote + attribution). It is the body on both page types, and both pages use it (7/7). siteRoot is the only root type, siteRoot→frontPage→blogPost, default templates are assigned, aliases are camelCase, and the grid is filed in Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid (5/5). No compositions. title/date/excerpt/listingImage are real properties on blogPost, and there are no duplicate or orphaned types (5/5). The image block has no alt field, so the caption doubles as alt text; too small to deduct.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: frontPage.cshtml and blogPost.cshtml call Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model.Body, "default"), the BlockGridModel overload of Umbraco's own renderer. That is fine, though (Model, "body") would match AGENTS.md more closely. There are no custom loops or parallel partials, and the scaffold's blockgrid partials are unchanged (7/7). Three adapters at Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml inherit UmbracoViewPage<BlockGridItem<T>>, map to plain models and call Component.InvokeAsync, with no markup (6/6). One ViewComponent per block (ViewComponents/*ViewComponent.cs) renders Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml. The views depend only on the plain models in Models/Blocks/ (7/7). Program.cs and appsettings.json are untouched, and there are no migrations and no Services. Children<BlogPost>(), Url() and GetCropUrl are the friendly extensions, nothing is injected, and Tailwind is built into dist/site.css through a shared _Layout (5/5).

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Two accurate, on-topic posts ('One Plug for Every AI Tool': N×M integrations, client/server split, reuse; 'for Teams': no copy-paste context, current data, per-server access control), each spread over five blocks with a relevant photo and a quote. They are still short: about 5–6 brief paragraphs, roughly 170–200 words of body each, and fairly generic (4/6). Clean, coherent Tailwind layout: a header, footer, max-w-3xl column, image cards on the listing, readable post typography, styled quote and figure captions, and a per-page <title> (4/4). The front page's intro and its text block say much the same thing twice.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Schema, media and domain went through the umbraco server, and pages, blocks and publishing through umbraco-editor (61 MCP calls, 37 writes). No migrations, Management API, uSync, DB or memory use. It followed steps 1–12 in order, with read-backs, get-property-value-template before the images, and stop/build before the Razor. Small deduction for writing curl scratch files to /tmp (front.html and both post pages), outside the project folder (2/3). The final report is mostly accurate and says what it didn't check. But its 'Conflict with AGENTS.md' section is wrong: it says the AGENTS.md example GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks") fails at runtime. In fact the model had written GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model.Body, "blocks"), passing a property alias as the template name. The AGENTS.md form, with this site's alias "body", works (1/2).

summary: A clean, fully working MCP-built blog: three well-modeled blocks (text, image, quote), correctly filed types, a domain on the front page, the exact adapter → ViewComponent pipeline, and a polished Tailwind layout. Points lost only for short posts, /tmp scratch files, and a final report that blames AGENTS.md for an error the model caused itself.
strengths: All 43 automated checks pass. Build has 0 warnings, and every page and image loads.
Schema is exactly right: blocks in Blocks, pages in Pages, siteRoot→frontPage→blogPost, the grid data type in Custom, no compositions.
Textbook block pipeline: Umbraco's GetBlockGridHtmlAsync, markup-free adapters, one ViewComponent per block, plain models in Models/Blocks/.
Polished layout with header, footer, image cards and styled quotes. Photo credits are in the captions.
Followed the numbered order of operations and only used the two MCP servers for schema and content.

issues.text: The final report's 'Conflict with AGENTS.md' says the documented GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks") fails. The 500 actually came from the model's own GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model.Body, "blocks"), which used the property alias as a template name. AGENTS.md is not wrong.
Posts are short, about 170–200 words of body each, with fairly generic content (/why-mcp-is-awesome-one-plug-for-every-ai-tool/, /why-mcp-is-awesome-for-teams-context-instead-of-copy-paste/).
Wrote curl scratch files to /tmp (front.html and both post HTML files), outside the project folder.

The front page's intro property and its block-grid text block repeat the same message (Views/frontPage.cshtml, /). The image block uses the caption, which includes the photo credit, as alt text (Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/imageBlock.cshtml).
